Expected goals (xG) is the probability that a shot becomes a goal, based on thousands of similar historical shots: distance, angle, body part, type of assist and game situation. A penalty is worth about 0.76 xG on Understat. Summing a player's or team's shot xG shows how many goals their chances were worth on average. Scoring more than your xG over a long run can mean excellent finishing or luck.
Non-penalty expected goals (npxG) is xG with penalties removed. It is a fairer way to compare attackers, because penalty duty inflates xG and goals for whoever takes them.
Expected assists (xA) is the xG of the shots a player sets up with a pass. It credits creating good chances even when the teammate misses.

xGChain is the total xG of every possession a player was involved in that ended in a shot, crediting each involved player with the full xG of the shot. xGBuildup is the same but excludes the shot and the key pass, so it rewards players involved earlier in moves, such as deep midfielders and ball-playing defenders.

PPDA (passes allowed per defensive action) measures pressing intensity: the number of passes the opponent completes in their own part of the pitch for each defensive action (tackle, interception, foul, challenge) by the pressing team. Lower PPDA means a more aggressive press. Values below about 9 indicate a high press; above about 13 a more passive block.
Deep completions are passes completed within roughly 20 metres of the opponent's goal, excluding crosses. They indicate how often a team gets the ball into dangerous areas.

A false nine is a centre-forward who drops deep into midfield instead of staying high against the centre-backs. It drags defenders out of position or creates an extra man in midfield, opening space for wingers and midfielders to run beyond. It suits technical forwards with good passing and teams that dominate possession.

A low block is a defensive shape where a team defends deep, close to its own penalty area, with compact lines and little space between them. It concedes possession to deny space behind the defence and often relies on counter-attacks.

A high press means pressuring the opponent's defenders and goalkeeper near their own goal to win the ball high up the pitch. Gegenpressing is the specific idea of pressing immediately after losing the ball, to win it back before the opponent can organise a counter.

An inverted full-back moves into central midfield when their team has the ball instead of overlapping on the wing. It adds a body in midfield, helps protect against counter-attacks and lets wingers hold the width.

A back three uses three central defenders, usually with wing-backs providing the width (3-4-3, 3-5-2, 3-4-2-1). It gives cover against central attacks and allows wing-backs to push high, but can leave space behind the wing-backs.

Overperforming xG means scoring more goals than expected from the quality of chances. Short runs of overperformance are common and often fade; elite finishers can sustain modest overperformance over several seasons. Comparing goals with npxG over at least 15 to 20 matches gives a fairer picture.

Per 90 statistics divide a total by minutes played and multiply by 90, so players with different playing time can be compared. Per-90 figures from fewer than about 600 minutes are noisy and should be treated with caution.
A clean sheet is a match in which a team concedes no goals.

The Pundit's statistics come from Understat (understat.com), refreshed weekly. It covers the Premier League, La Liga, Serie A, Bundesliga and Ligue 1 for the 2026-27 season. Live in-game data is not included.
